title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) / Indian Penal Code (IPC) — Criminal Law Provisions
content:
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023 came into force on 1 July 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860 as the primary criminal law statute of India. It defines criminal offences and prescribes statutory penalties for acts committed within Indian territory.

The BNS 2023 covers offences against public order, offences affecting the human body, offences against property, and financial/electronic fraud.

Theft & Robbery: Theft is defined under Section 303 BNS (formerly Section 378 IPC) as dishonestly taking movable property out of the possession of any person without their consent. Punishments include up to 3 years imprisonment or fine. Robbery is aggravated theft accompanied by force or threat under Section 309 BNS (formerly Section 390 IPC).

Cheating & Financial Fraud: Cheating is defined under Section 318 BNS (formerly Section 415 & 420 IPC) as deceiving any person to deliver property or alter records. Maximum punishment for cheating is up to 7 years imprisonment with fine. Cheating by personation (Section 319 BNS / Section 416 IPC) applies to impersonation and online identity theft.

Criminal Breach of Trust: Defined under Section 316 BNS (formerly Section 405 IPC). It applies when a person entrusted with property or financial funds dishonestly misappropriates or converts it. This covers employee financial fraud, unauthorized diversion of funds, and breach of fiduciary custody.

FIR Registration (BNSS 2023): Registration of a First Information Report (FIR) for any cognisable offence is mandatory under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023 (formerly Section 154 CrPC). Complaints for online financial fraud or theft can also be submitted online via the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in).
